title: Senate Republicans Want $1 Billion to Make Trump's Ballroom Super Safe
summary: Imagine a party at the White House, but someone tries to sneak in with weapons. That scary thing almost happened last week at a media dinner where President Trump was speaking. A man named Cole Tomas Allen was charged with trying to assassinate the president. Now, Senate Republicans want to spend $1 billion to make the White House safer—especially a new ballroom Trump wants to build. The ballroom is part of a big construction project on the East Wing. The White House says it will have bomb shelters, military rooms, and even a medical facility underneath. Trump says it needs bulletproof glass and should stop drone attacks. The $1 billion would go to the Secret Service for 'security adjustments and upgrades,' but it can't be used for non-security parts like fancy decorations. The money is part of a larger bill to fund immigration agencies, which Democrats have been blocking. Some Republicans say after the dinner attack, the president needs a secure place to host events. 'It would be insane' to hold the dinner at a hotel again, said Senator Lindsey Graham. But Democrats are angry. Senator Dick Durbin said, 'While Americans are struggling to make ends meet, Republicans are focused on providing tens of billions of dollars for the President's vanity ballroom project.' A court has allowed construction to continue while a historic preservation group sues to stop it.
why_it_matters: Decisions about spending huge amounts of tax money affect how much is left for schools, roads, and other things that matter to your community.

background_read: The White House East Wing is where big official parties are held; the Secret Service, created to protect the president, has guarded it since the 1800s.
The last time a president was shot and survived was Ronald Reagan in 1981, which prompted stronger security measures.
Historic preservation groups (groups that protect old buildings) can sue to block construction if they think it will harm a historic place.

perspectives.description: The $1 billion upgrade could make the White House much safer for future events, preventing another attack.
Spending so much on a ballroom when many families struggle with high prices seems like a misuse of taxpayer funds.
This fight is part of a constant struggle between modern security needs and keeping old buildings as they were.
